subject: Post-call summary — BrightData workloads & Dedicated fit
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Tania Morales <tania@brightdata.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-15T13:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call summary — BrightData workloads & Dedicated fit

Thanks again for carving out time today, Tania — good conversation. Below is a concise summary of what we discussed, the immediate pain we heard, and suggested next steps so we can keep momentum.

TL;DR
- Primary ask: reduce per-token cost and meet peak-throughput SLA for browser-scrape RAG workloads (latency < 300ms P95 for 1k concurrent users).
- Current environment: BrightData running several 7B/13B models in prod via public cloud with high egress and variable latency spikes.
- Recommended short path: 2-week Dedicated pilot on instance type X with prefix/KV caching + 4:1 batching to validate 40% cost reduction and stable P95 latency.

Pain points & evidence
- Latency spikes during concurrent ingestion windows (logs show P95 latency 600–900ms).
- Token cost variability due to lack of shared caching and small batch sizes.
- Compliance requirement: all inference logs retained for 30 days in their EU region for one business line (we noted this will require Private/VPC consideration for that subset).

Goals we captured
1) Prove cost reduction: target 30–50% lower per-token cost vs current baseline.
2) Meet latency SLO: P95 < 300ms under 1k concurrent users for read-heavy RAG queries.
3) Organize procurement/contract timeline to allow production transition by Q4.

Proposed pilot outline (what Redwood will deliver)
- 2-week Dedicated pilot with a dedicated GPU pool and pre-configured caching and batching rules.
- Measurement plan: we provide a usage snapshot and a dashboard (token-level cost, latency breakdown, cache hit rate).
- Optional: a short quantization experiment on the 13B model to show additional cost savings (non-blocking for pilot go-live).

Next steps / asks
- BrightData to confirm pilot scope and which workload to mirror (browser-scrape RAG + one classification pipeline). Target: confirm by 2027-06-18.
- Jordan/Monica to share Dedicated pilot proposal and a short usage snapshot (attached).
- Procurement contact to flag any required security docs ahead of pilot (SOC2 evidence, data residency addendum).

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-proposal.pdf (proposal + measurement plan), brightdata-usage-q2-snapshot.csv (anonymized token counts and latencies)

Thanks — I’ll follow up with the proposal and a stub SOW for procurement.

—
Jordan Blake
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0134

Redwood Inference — developer-first inference runtime
From: Tania Morales <tania@brightdata.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-15T15:01:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call summary — BrightData workloads & Dedicated fit

Appreciate the write-up, Jordan — that aligns with our internal read. A few clarifications: 

1) Pilot scope: agree on browser-scrape RAG + classification. For the RAG workload, we want the pilot to include our nightly bulk reindex window (that tends to cause the latency spikes).
2) Data residency: we have two business units; only EU-sensitive traffic needs VPC. The pilot can run in us-west for the non-sensitive unit — we still need to see how logs can be forwarded for the EU unit.
3) Procurement: looping in procurement (procurement@brightdata.ai) to start paperwork. We’ll need an outline of required controls and a sample SOC2 report.

Can you also include an expected price band for the 2-week pilot (ballpark numbers) so the finance folks can sign off quickly?

I’ll check internally on resource availability for the week of 6/28 (preferred) or 7/5 (backup).

Thanks — Tania
Tania Morales
Head of Product Operations, BrightData Labs
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Tania Morales <tania@brightdata.ai>, Procurement <procurement@brightdata.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-16T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call summary — BrightData workloads & Dedicated fit

Tania / Procurement — thanks. Quick responses and an initial price band below so finance has something to react to: 

Pilot pricing (ballpark; final quote in attached PDF)
- 2-week Dedicated pilot + infra + monitoring: $18,000 — $28,000 depending on GPU class and included burst capacity.
- Optional quantization experiment / model tuning (one-off effort): $6,000.
- SOC2 evidence & security package: provided at no extra cost for pilots; for Private/VPC we’ll surface any infra charges separately.

Operational notes
- Monica will own onboarding and measurement. Monica: I’ll schedule a 30-min kickoff once Tania confirms the pilot start week.
- Expected deliverables: pilot SOW, measurement dashboard access, weekly sync notes, final pilot report with cost/latency delta.

Procurement: we’ve attached a sample SOW and the proposal PDF. If you need a PO template, flag it.

Next dates to lock
- Confirm pilot scope & start week: 2027-06-18 (Tania)
- Kickoff meeting (30m): week of 2027-06-28 (if confirmed)

—
Jordan Blake
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-16T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call summary — BrightData workloads & Dedicated fit

Got it — I’ll prepare the onboarding checklist and a lightweight dashboard template for the pilot metrics (token-level cost, cache hit %, P95 latency). I’ll also include the minimal AWS/GCP/network requirements and a runbook for the nightly reindex window test.

I’ll aim to have the kickoff invite and dashboard link ready by EOD 2027-06-17 so Jordan can share with BrightData.
